subject: TTL budgeting and staged certificate rotation for peered VPC private endpoints
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Chang <samuel.chang@bluepeak.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TTL budgeting and staged certificate rotation for peered VPC private endpoints

Team —

We need to finalize a low-risk plan to rotate TLS certs for the private endpoints that sit behind the BluePeak peering links. Primary constraints from the customer: they run long-lived client connections from internal agents (some process-level pinning), they use private hosted zones in Route-like systems, and their client cache TTLs vary across regions.

Proposal (high level):
- Create a TTL budget per FQDN (see attached dns-ttl-budget-matrix.xlsx).
- Stage rotation in two waves: control plane endpoints first (low-traffic), then tenant-facing endpoints.
- Use a grace period where both old and new certs are served (SNI-based pick), with a 72h monitoring window and explicit rollback triggers.
- Coordinate DNS TTL changes: lower TTL to 300s 48h prior to rotation, perform rotation, then raise TTL back after confirmation.

Open questions for BluePeak:
1) Do any clients perform certificate pinning with OS-level caches that may ignore DNS TTL?
2) Are there any global NAT or proxy caches between our peered VPCs that would hold an old cert beyond the DNS TTL?

Action items I want by EOD: Laura, review the TTL budget sheet and confirm per-endpoint suggested values. Marissa, can you draft a rollback checklist and a monitoring playbook (alerts + synthetic checks)? Samuel — please confirm whether BluePeak has any intermediary caches and whether they can lower their side TTLs to 60s for the maintenance window.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dns-ttl-budget-matrix.xlsx
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTL budgeting and staged certificate rotation for peered VPC private endpoints

Jonas —

Reviewed the matrix and added notes in column G for client-observed behavior. Quick notes:
- Control plane endpoints: TTL can be 60s for the window. Most control clients poll/refresh and tolerate rapid changes.
- Tenant endpoints: we should target 300s for the staged window, 60s only if BluePeak confirms no mid-path caches.
- Client pinning: I flagged two services that ship with pinned cert bundles (see rows 12 and 19). Those require coordinated agent updates or a dual-cert acceptance window on the client.

Draft rollback checklist (high level):
1) Immediately revert to serving only old cert via the proxy routing policy.
2) Re-announce original records (if any DNS changes were made) and set TTL back to previous value.
3) Trigger synthetic end-to-end checks and open incident ticket.
4) Escalate to BluePeak ops if any cross-peering caches are suspected.

I can expand these into a runbook for the rotation run (I’ll drop a PDF). Marissa — loop me into the monitoring rule names when you publish them so I can sanity-check thresholds.

-Laura

From: Samuel Chang <samuel.chang@bluepeak.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2026 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTL budgeting and staged certificate rotation for peered VPC private endpoints

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads-up. A few clarifications from BluePeak ops:
- We do have an L7 caching appliance in the transit layer for a small subset of flows (legacy support). It respects Origin TTL but sometimes holds connections up to 30m under heavy load.
- We can lower our side TTLs to 60s for the maintenance window; request must be made 24h beforehand.
- No client-side pinning on our managed services side, but several of their downstream customers (integrators) do pin. We recommend the dual-cert acceptance period of at least 48h to give them time to update bundles.

We can join a 30m sync at 10:00 PT tomorrow to walk the cutover steps and confirm monitoring hooks.

—Samuel
Senior Cloud Ops Engineer
BluePeak Communications

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samuel Chang <samuel.chang@bluepeak.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTL budgeting and staged certificate rotation for peered VPC private endpoints

All —

Updated runbook attached (rotation-runbook-v1.pdf). Summary of changes based on feedback:
- Per-endpoint TTLs set in the attached matrix; control-plane endpoints: 60s, tenant-frontends: 300s default with a conditional 60s if BluePeak confirms no transit cache.
- Dual-cert serving window: 72h with active synthetic validation every 5m.
- Rollback triggers: >2% request error spike sustained for 15m, or any SNI mismatch reported by synthetic checks.
- Pre-change checklist: lower DNS TTLs 48h prior, notify all integrators, schedule maintenance sync with BluePeak and Compliance.

Next steps:
- Samuel: confirm the 10:00 PT sync and whether BluePeak can proactively notify integrator contacts on our behalf.
- Laura: finalize the agent update plan for the two pinned clients listed in the matrix.
- Jonas: approve the runbook and I’ll schedule an incident drill.

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rotation-runbook-v1.pdf, dns-ttl-budget-matrix.xlsx
